An unflinching,
first-person narrative.

Part confession, part atonement, part love letter to the sheer stubbornness of survival, Groove is a raw, funny, and fiercely honest account of moving through the world — the wounds we inherit, the ruts we get stuck in, and the groove we learn to move in.

About the author

Adrienne Ford writes with a confessional candor that refuses to beg.

She narrates suicidal ideation, assault, and church shame in a wry, unsentimental voice that thinks in reclaimed wordplay and extended metaphor — intimate, culturally rooted, and funny at the very edge of grief. Groove is a survivor's account that never asks for pity, only for the truth to finally be said out loud: the difference between a rut and a rhythm, and the long way home to yourself.

Unflinching and unexpectedly hilarious, she's a light back for anyone who's ever felt themselves disappearing. Find your groove

You're not alone.

If today feels heavy, reach out. These are free, confidential, and always open.

988Suicide & Crisis Lifeline — call or text 988, any time (U.S.). RAINNSexual assault support — 1-800-656-4673, and online chat. Find a HelplineCrisis lines in your country, worldwide. Therapy for Black GirlsFind a therapist and a community that gets it. The Loveland FoundationTherapy support for Black women and girls. NAMIMental health education, support, and local resources.
